title: MicroCT-Based Additive Manufacturing Quality Control: Porosity Analysis
author: Anton Du Plessis
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.sc7eazn

steps.title: Prepare Sample
steps.instruction: Use a standard coupon sample of 10 x 10 x 10 mm (e.g., SLM produced Ti-6Al-4V).

steps.title: Mount Sample
steps.instruction: Load the sample in foam at an angle of roughly 10-45 degrees to ensure no edge artefacts are present.

steps.title: Perform MicroCT Scan
steps.instruction: Perform MicroCT using a standard laboratory microCT system with the following settings:

substeps.instruction: Set voltage to 200 kV and current to 70 uA.
Set image acquisition to 500 ms per image.
Perform a full 360 degree rotation with 2400 step positions.
At each step position, discard the first image and average two subsequent images.

steps.title: Reconstruct Images
steps.instruction: Reconstruct the scan data using a strong beam hardening correction factor without any image de-noising.

steps.title: Segment Exterior Air
steps.instruction: Using Volume Graphics VGStudioMax 3.1 software, remove exterior air to create an accurate segmentation of the cube edge.

substeps.instruction: Create a region of interest (ROI) from this surface.
Modify the ROI using an opening/closing function with a value of +3 and create a new ROI to close small surface pores.
Use a region growing tool with high tolerance on the air surrounding the part, selecting the 'avoid other visible ROIs' option (ensure 'volume' is highlighted and ROI is visible).
If loose powder/noise particles are present outside the part, apply an opening/closing function (+3) to this region to remove them.
Invert the exterior-air selection to select the entire part including internal voids.
Apply a new advanced surface determination function using this ROI selection as a starting contour for local optimization.

steps.title: Extract Sub-surface Region
steps.instruction: Create a sub-surface ROI to eliminate open edge pores and surface roughness errors.

substeps.instruction: Use 'select ROI from surface' to create an ROI.
Go to selection modes 'erode/dilate' and erode the sample by -2 voxels.
Create a new volume and extract the ROI.

steps.title: Analyze Porosity and Voids
steps.instruction: Perform quantitative defect analysis on the extracted sub-surface region.

substeps.instruction: Apply a new advanced surface determination to the material/defect interface regions using the sub-surface ROI.

Manually select the interface threshold in a contrasted slice view with the preview function to ensure proper selection between pore space and material (if no voids are visible, select the threshold to the left of the material peak).
Invert the selected region to highlight only void spaces.
Use the inverted region as a defect mask in the porosity analysis function.
